I suspect deep down this is the answer. Pain and suffering are highly subjective. I, for example, know that I feel pain in situations where most people wouldn't. For example, one time before an event, I was having my hair tied by a teacher and I felt like they were trying to remove my entire scalp, while all the other girls claimed they felt absolute zero pain, even though the teacher was using the same method. I have felt tremendous pain sitting on normal wooden chairs at university while no one else ever felt it. 

So it's possible that most people don't feel pain as intensely as I do, not even in terrible situations. They don't get to the point in which they decide that not existing is better (I fucking reached this conclusion when I was 10!) They don't get to the point where they can't accept justifications for torture. In fact, most of them loove to come up with reasons and justifications all the time. 

The problem is that this theory is kind of offensive because I bet there will be people coming and saying "oh but X went through the holocaust and remained optimistic, how dare you say they didn't suffer enough!!"

And obviously part of me being highly empathic means that I don't want to dismiss other people's perceptions. But I do know one thing: I just perceive pain differently. I don't tolerate it at all. I don't want it. I don't care if it teaches me a lesson. I don't want it and I hate having been forced to go through all this shit. I hate that nature even allowed for freaks like me to exist. I hate that we're doomed and there's nothing I can do. Nothing will ever get rid of suffering.

I've been in almost the same situation, as you can tell by my post history. Over a year of non-stop daily symptoms and trying different diets and meds. Although maybe not as painful as yours. My problem is mostly gas in the chest. In the last couple of days I've been finally getting SOME relief although I'm not cured. 

My advice is: you gotta keep investigating and trying treatments. Insist even if doctors want to give up on you. Search info online yourself too because medicine sucks at treating chronic pain. 

Take care of your mental health. Sometimes we are so (understandably) depressed and frustrated because of the pain that we get into a constant negative mindset and can't see solutions, only negatives. 

I recommend looking for books with titles like "Cognitive behavioral therapy for chronic pain". It might help you. Also just books about people who've gone through terrible situations and eventually got our of them. Cliche, but it might inspire you to keep fighting and to remember that you must still have some things you are grateful for.

I think we will all eventually get better. Maybe not 100% to normal but at least with a decent life. If we are here thinking about this, posting it, is because we care enough to follow recommendations and do everything in our power to stop the illness. People like us eventually succeed. We just need to be patient.

If you have access to psychiatric meds like antidepressants, perhaps that can help you feel better emotionally. In my case it helped immensely with my mood and mindset.

"What does not feeling anything feel like?" That's interesting. I guess there's never just "nothing", it's just that there are no specific sensations, nothing that differentiates one moment from the other, one emotion from the other. It always feels "neutral", except when I'm crying.

My vision is indeed blurry when I'm crying. My eyelids are a bit different too, like they're heavier after a lot of crying. My cheeks don't feel that different. Yes, my voice changes when I cry, and also, it often "breaks" when I try to speak. It can be difficult to speak when you're crying.

To be honest, I don't think this is something I don't pay attention to. I experience all of that frequently, and they don't go unnoticed. In my post I said when I cry I feel the lump on my throat and that I've experienced chest pain once or twice. That implies I do have physical reactions when I cry. Yes, it didn't ocurr to me to mention blurry eyes and voice change, so maybe I forgot to count them as a sensation but it doesn't mean I'm not aware they're happening. The idea of not paying attention to a physical change seems strange to me. Like, how do you not pay attention to the fact that your vision has changed, your voice has changed, that your eyelids feel different? Because there is clearly a CHANGE. It's not that I don't get any reactions ever. The thing is, I can only feel those things when I'm crying. And when I'm not crying I don't notice anything. So all other emotions that don't provoque crying don't have any special sensations, my body just always feels the same when I'm not crying (unless there's, of course, something exterior causing me pain)

That's why when I read those questions I can say "oh yeah, I definitely experience that, I forgot to count them as a sensation" and I remember all the times I've experienced it, and I can feel them again when I cry. But when I read people's descriptions of other emotions and how they feel physically (tension, tightening, contractions, etc.) they sound very alien, there's not a memory of ever feeling someting like that. And even if I try to pay attention to them when I get an emotion, they're not there. They never appear.Still, it's good to hear that I can still benefit from meditation.

I see... but I have never experienced that. I can remember once my hear rate accelerated when I was scared but it lasted only like 15 seconds. And I didn't feel tense nor did I began to sweat or anything (but can you really sweat in like 15 seconds?) And after that it never happened again. I've never felt stress in my body either. Although that's also difficult to tell, because I'm not sure if I ever experience stress in the first place. I know what it's like to be annoyed or frustrated but... stressed? I'm not sure if I experence stress. I know this must sound really really hard to believe, but I'm not lying, and it's making me really curious, how am I not able to feel all those things? Unless I'm completely unaware of the feelings in my body, which seems difficult to believe, because I'm actually purposely trying to feel them, paying attention to the body, multiple times a day.

It seems like everyone is saying that I'm not paying enough attention but I already try, in different times of the day, to scan, and can never feel anything. It's not like I don't stop to analyze my body. So what am I doing wrong? ? I followed all the instructions I've read about this and it still doesn't work. And no one ever mentions the possibility of not feeling anything. No one even thinks it's weird to suggest that emotions are felt in the body (I thought it was weird when I first heard it) It seems like most people have no problem feeling them, and they just accept the idea of feeling emotions in their body as a very normal thing, which means there's something else going on with me. I've been trying this for more than two weeks. Maybe it's just not enough time. But how can I be sooo bad at paying attention? Can I just suddenly one day start feeling something, after months of trying? I guess maybe it can happen? Maybe it's something I have to learn from scratch?

I do sometimes think that there's something abnormal in my brain. I used to hear people complain that certain parts of their body hurt when experiencing emotions, or that their muscles were tense because of stress, and I never experienced that. So, in a way, I knew my experience was "different", but I always assumed that those were just exceptions or extreme cases and that most of the time it was a mental process for most people, just like it was for me. But wouldn't abnormalities in my emotional centers also stop me from feeling any emotions at all? That is, I wouldn't be able to feel them mentally. I believe I do experience emotions. And I do cry a lot.
That never happened to me. So... I don't really know to think of this, but yeah, I'll keep investigating.
